handoga.name: Handoga
handoga.summary: An archaeological site west of Dikhil, Djibouti, where 1970 excavations found the foundations of stone houses and a stone building facing Mecca.

dhambalin.name: Dhambalin
dhambalin.summary: A sandstone rock-shelter site in Somaliland, discovered in 2007, with rock art of cattle, goats, and giraffes, and the earliest known images of sheep in the region, dated to about 5000 years ago.

sahil-somaliland.name: Sahil
sahil-somaliland.summary: An administrative region of northern Somaliland with the port city of Berbera as its capital, created in 1991 and expanded in 1998, bordering the Gulf of Aden.

laas-geel.name: Laas Geel
laas-geel.summary: Cave formations near Hargeisa, Somaliland, containing some of the earliest known cave paintings of domesticated cattle in the Horn of Africa, estimated at 4,500 to 5,500 years old.

hargeisa.name: Hargeisa
hargeisa.summary: Capital and largest city of Somaliland, founded as an Isaaq watering and trading stop and now a commercial hub in the Ogo highlands.

somaliland.name: Somaliland
somaliland.summary: A partially recognised state in the Horn of Africa with about 6.2 million people, which declared independence from Somalia in 1991 after a decade-long war.

hararghe.name: Hararghe
hararghe.summary: Former province of eastern Ethiopia whose capital was the city of Harar.

dire-dawa.name: Dire Dawa
dire-dawa.summary: City in eastern Ethiopia, one of only two chartered cities in the country (with the capital Addis Ababa), and today an industrial centre with major markets.

nataruk.name: Nataruk
nataruk.summary: An archaeological site in Kenya where the remains of 27 people, dated to about 9,500–10,500 years ago, show signs of violent death, seen by some as the earliest evidence of prehistoric warfare.

turkana-county.name: Turkana County
turkana-county.summary: Kenya's largest county by land area, in the northwest bordering Uganda, South Sudan, Ethiopia and Lake Turkana; home to the Turkana people, with a 2019 population of about 927,000.

lake-turkana.name: Lake Turkana
lake-turkana.summary: A saline lake in Kenya's Rift Valley, the world's largest permanent desert lake and largest alkaline lake, now threatened by dam construction upstream in Ethiopia.

rachel-wood-archaeologist.name: Rachel Wood
rachel-wood-archaeologist.summary: An archaeologist specializing in radiocarbon dating of Pleistocene sites, and director of the Oxford Radiocarbon Accelerator Unit at the University of Oxford.

cushitic-speaking-peoples.name: Cushitic-speaking peoples
cushitic-speaking-peoples.summary: Ethnolinguistic groups who speak Cushitic languages natively, found mainly in the Horn of Africa with smaller communities in Egypt, Sudan, Kenya and Tanzania.

itbay.name: Red Sea Hills
itbay.summary: A chain of mountains running parallel to the Red Sea in southeastern Egypt and northeastern Sudan, separating the coastal plain from the Eastern Desert.

atbarah-river.name: Atbarah River
atbarah-river.summary: River in northeast Africa rising in Ethiopia and flowing about 805 km to join the Nile in Sudan, the last tributary the Nile receives before reaching the Mediterranean.

mereb-river.name: Mereb (Gash) River
mereb-river.summary: A river flowing from central Eritrea, also called the Gash River, that today forms part of the border between Eritrea and Ethiopia.

pastoral-neolithic.name: Pastoral Neolithic
pastoral-neolithic.summary: A period in East African prehistory (from about 5,000 years ago) marking the start of herding and pottery use, built on nomadic pastoralism rather than farming.

ensete-ventricosum.name: Enset
ensete-ventricosum.summary: Banana-family plant, also called the false banana, cultivated only in Ethiopia, where it is a staple food for roughly 20 million people.

kassala.name: Kassala
kassala.summary: The capital of Kassala state in eastern Sudan, on the Gash River, known for its fruit gardens and as a market and trade hub near the Eritrean border.

butana-group.name: Butana Group
butana-group.summary: A Neolithic culture in eastern Sudan flourishing from about 4000 to 2900 BC, known for decorated pottery, stone tools, and animal herding.

african-humid-period.name: African humid period
african-humid-period.summary: A wetter climate phase in Africa during the late Pleistocene and Holocene, when the Sahara was covered in grasses, trees and lakes, lasting roughly from 14,600 to about 5,000 years ago.

aurochs.name: Aurochs
aurochs.summary: An extinct wild ancestor of domestic cattle, once found from western Europe to East Asia, with the last known individual dying in the late 17th or early 18th century.

jarigole-pillar-site.name: Jarigole Pillar Site
jarigole-pillar-site.summary: A megalithic communal cemetery near Lake Turkana in Kenya, built by early pastoral herders around 5,000 years ago and used for burials over a few centuries.

great-rift-valley.name: Great Rift Valley
great-rift-valley.summary: A roughly 6,500-kilometre series of connected geographic depressions running from Syria through the Red Sea to Mozambique, a term introduced by geologist John Walter Gregory in 1896.

nubia.name: Nubia
nubia.summary: A region along the Nile between Khartoum and Aswan, seat of ancient civilizations including the Kerma culture and the Kingdom of Kush, which conquered Egypt in the 8th century BC.

gash-group.name: Gash Group
gash-group.summary: A Neolithic culture that flourished from about 3000 to 1800 BCE in Eritrea and eastern Sudan, named for the Gash river.

jebel-mokram-group.name: Jebel Mokram Group
jebel-mokram-group.summary: A prehistoric Neolithic culture in eastern Sudan and western Eritrea that flourished from around 1800 BCE, known for its distinctive incised pottery and small clay animal figures.

waaq.name: Waaqism
waaq.summary: The pre-Muslim monotheistic faith of Cushitic peoples of the Horn of Africa, centered on Waaq, the sky god, whose name still means 'God' in Oromo.

wilton-culture.name: Wilton culture
wilton-culture.summary: Archaeologists' term for sites and cultures sharing similar stone-tool technology dating from about 8,000 to 4,000 years ago, treated as a technocomplex.

land-of-punt.name: Land of Punt
land-of-punt.summary: An ancient kingdom known from Egyptian trade records for gold, resins, ebony, ivory and wild animals, likely located in the Horn of Africa; Egyptians called it 'Land of the God'.

donald-n-levine.name: Donald N. Levine
donald-n-levine.summary: American sociologist (1931–2015) at the University of Chicago known for his sociological theory, translations of Georg Simmel, and work as a central figure in Ethiopian Studies.

proto-cushitic-language.name: Proto-Cushitic
proto-cushitic-language.summary: The reconstructed common ancestor of the Cushitic language family, possibly originating in the Red Sea Hills, with no scholarly consensus on its exact homeland.

cushitic-languages.name: Cushitic languages
cushitic-languages.summary: Branch of the Afroasiatic language family spoken mainly in the Horn of Africa; major languages include Oromo, Somali, Beja, Afar, Hadiyya, Kambaata and Sidama.
